---

### 1. `data_quality` — **completed** | confidence **high**
**Findings.** CGM is usable for pattern work. 3995 valid entries, 0 invalid, 0 duplicates, cadence ~5 min, coverage **98.7%**, 10 gaps, largest gap **65 min**, period 14 d (07-Aug 21:13Z → 21-Aug 21:13Z), local TZ **BST**. Device-status volume is rich (6214). Loop samples show closed loop throughout the representative set.

**Evidence.** `telemetry.data_quality.status=good`; first/last entry inside the window; `included_counts` supplies 15 daily rows, 24 local hourly rows, 16 extremes, 24 therapy windows, 40 representative treatments, 24 loop statuses, 27 events.

**Supportable later inferences.** Overnight/local-hour glucose shape; hypo/hyper extremes; that carbs are not in Nightscout; that UAM/SMB are active with COB=0 in sampled loop reasons.

**Not supportable as isolated profile defects.** Daytime basal vs meal vs UAM; CR fit; composition of “Correction Bolus” vs meal insulin; pre-13-Aug vs post-switch behavior without splitting the fortnight.

**Data gaps.** `carb_entries=0`, `total_carbs_g=0`, `carb_treatment_entries=[]`; no meal-strategy declaration; treatments included are a sample (40 of 2315); loop statuses are a sample (24 of 6214); no activity stream; profile switch 13-Aug 21:23 and site/sensor/occlusion events interrupt stationarity; u200 dilution is named but not quantified in units-of-U100.

**Hypotheses.** H-DQ1: daytime glucose is UAM-driven unlogged intake, not a clean basal test. H-DQ2: mid-period profile/site change and GLP-1 notes mean the 14-day average mixes regimes.

---

### 2. `safety_overview` — **completed** | confidence **high** (patterns), **medium** (cause)
**Findings.** Overall TIR **86%**, TAR **8.9%**, TBR **5.1%**, mean **121.6**, SD **39.7**, CV **32.6%** (variability above a typical ~33% caution line). Safety constraint for all later steps: **recurrent hypoglycemia**, including severe readings, plus same-day high/low swings.

**Hypoglycemia (must limit later changes).**
- Local hours with TBR ≥10%: **01:00 18.5%**, **00:00 11.4%**, **19:00 15.3%**, **02–03 ~10%**, **23:00 10.1%**.
- Clustered extremes: 13-Aug ~17:00Z (51→42), 14-Aug ~18:05Z (48→41), 21-Aug 06:19Z (**42**).
- High-TBR days: 11-Aug 9.4%, 14-Aug 8.3%, **18-Aug 12.8%**.

**Hyperglycemia.** Afternoon/evening TAR: local **16:00 32.1%**, 14:00 26.3%, 15:00 23.6%, 17:00 22.6%, 10:00 20.2%. Extremes 15-Aug ~16:30Z **293**, 18-Aug ~12:00Z **290**. 14-Aug TAR 20.8% then evening low 41.

**Other safety context.** Occlusion + pump error 19-Aug 13:40; GLP-1 1.25 mg notes 14/17/20-Aug; SMB always + UAM; max IOB 25 U / max basal 12 U/h are very high vs ~0.5–0.8 U/h scheduled basal; sampled IOB at highs **4.7–5.9 U** with aggressive DynISF (variable_sens ~28–38 vs profile 56).

**Hypotheses.**  
H-S1: Early-night lows = residual evening insulin (UAM/SMB + corrections) + target 90 from 23:00, not proven overnight basal excess alone.  
H-S2: 18–19 local crash = delayed action after 14–17 highs (stacking), sometimes after large/manual corrections (e.g. 14-Aug 16:20 0.2 U window start 234 → 56 at 120 min; 19-Aug 15:55 0.65 U start 264 → 96).  
H-S3: DynISF 70% + SMB always amplifies both afternoon catch-up and overshoot.  
H-S4: GLP-1 may increase evening hypo risk and reduce oral intake (consistent with zero logged carbs).  
H-S5: 21-Aug 06:19 low of 42 is not the dominant 06:00-hour pattern (local 06–07 TBR 2.5% / 1.3%).

**Dependencies.** Relies on data_quality (coverage good; carb absence means hypo cause is mixed).

**Uncertainty / gaps.** No hypo treatment logs; no activity; cannot quantify how much of TBR is loop zero-temp vs basal vs SMB; dilution/peak model vs DIA 10 h unverified.

**Constraint carried forward:** do not propose stronger overnight insulin, lower ISF, or more SMB until early-night and evening hypo explanations are separated.

---

### 3. `basal_targets` — **partial** | confidence **medium** overnight / **low** daytime
**Findings by local time vs segments.**

| Window (local) | Glucose | Scheduled | Target | Interpretation |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 23–03 | Mean 90–106, TBR 10–18% | 0.7 then 0.6 from 00:00 | 90 from 23:00 | Possible mild overnight insulin pressure **or** evening IOB carryover into a tight target |
| 04–07 | Mean ~99–106, TIR 95–99% | 0.6 → 0.7@05 → 0.8@06 | 90 | Fasting-like and **stable**; 06:00 0.8 looks adequate, not clearly high |
| 08–09 | Rise 110 → 133, TAR 2–9% | 0.8 then 0.7@10 | 100 from 08:00 | Compatible with breakfast / UAM, not a clean basal defect |
| 10–13 | Mean 132–148, TAR 8–17% | 0.7 | 100 | Meal/UAM plausible |
| 14–17 | Mean 148–163, TAR 23–32% | 0.7 then **0.5@16** | 100 | Highs **before and after** the 16:00 basal drop; cannot blame 0.5 U/h as the primary afternoon peak |
| 18–19 | Mean 124 → 105, TBR 8% then **15%** | 0.5 → 0.6@18 → 0.7@19 | 100 | Rebound/late insulin more plausible than under-basal |
| 20–22 | Mean 117–128, mixed TAR/TBR | 0.7 | 100 then 90@23 | Unstable; likely dinner/UAM |

**Targets.** Overnight 90 is tight relative to CV 32.6% and hour-01 TBR 18.5%. Day target 100 sits under a large afternoon mean (not proof the target is “wrong”).

**Competing explanations (not resolved).**  
A) 00:00 basal 0.6 slightly high and/or 19:00 0.7 too high into the night.  
B) Basal OK; evening UAM/SMB + DIA 10 h + DynISF overshoot into target 90.  
C) GLP-1 / unlogged low intake after afternoon insulin.  
D) Site/occlusion days (10, 13, 17, 19) distort a few nights.

**What is not labeled a basal defect.** Afternoon TAR (COB always 0 in loop samples; UAM boost language; zero carb diary). The 16:00 basal reduction sits **inside** the peak, so raising afternoon basal would be premature and hypo-adjacent to the 18–19 crash.

**Dependencies.** Safety_overview hypo constraint; data_quality carb gap.

**Data gaps.** No fasting experiment / temp-target-only nights isolated; representative temps include many 0 U/h and high temps, so the loop is already rewriting basal continuously; profile switch 13-Aug.

**Uncertainty.** Medium that *something* in the 23:00–03:00 insulin+target package is slightly aggressive; low that any single basal row should move before automation (SMB/UAM/DynISF) is reviewed in step 2.

---

### 4. `profile_cr_isf_dia` — **partial** | confidence **low** CR, **medium** ISF/DIA as a system
**CR.** Five segments (13 / 11.1 / 13.2 / 10.5 / 12.6) **cannot be validated**. Zero carb entries, `smb_with_cob_enabled=false`, loop `cob: 0` in every sampled status. Therapy windows are labeled Correction Bolus and often show rises after insulin (unlogged food) or collapses too large for the listed bolus (other IOB/loop). **CR change is blocked**, not “keep because it fits.”

**ISF.** Flat **56 mg/dL/U**. Loop `variable_sens` in samples spans ~28–124, i.e. DynISF (70%) is the *effective* ISF. At highs, reasons show ISF ~1.5–3 mmol-scale (~27–54 mg/dL/U). Observed 120–240 min drops after small listed boluses are inconsistent with 56 acting alone and consistent with stacked SMB + much stronger dynamic ISF. Night/low-BG samples show *weaker* variable_sens (higher mg/dL/U), which is expected with DynISF and argues against blaming a “too strong flat 56” for overnight lows without the automation layer.

**DIA 10 h** + `free_peak_oref`. Long DIA reduces apparent IOB decay and can leave conservative IOB on the books, but sampled IOB still reached 4.7–5.9 U at 245–262 mg/dL — so delivery is not DIA-limited in those scenes. Evening delayed lows are compatible with long tail **or** late UAM SMBs; those are not separable here.

**System view.** Profile ISF 56 + CR unused + UAM-only meals + DynISF 70% + SMB always means **meal and correction behavior is almost entirely automation**, not wizard CR/ISF. Changing CR or ISF now would not be identifiable and could interact with DynISF.

**Hypotheses.**  
H-P1: Afternoon highs = no carb announcement + UAM lag, not a weak 08:00/16:00 CR.  
H-P2: Flat ISF is a seed for DynISF; apparent “ISF too weak by day / too strong by night” may be DynISF + SMB, not the 56 seed.  
H-P3: DIA 10 h may be intentional for dilute/u200; evidence neither confirms nor refutes misfit.  
H-P4: 04:00 CR 11.1 is unused in practice if no carbs are entered overnight.

**Dependencies.** Basal/target unresolved for overnight; safety hypo cap; carb gap.

**Data gaps.** No meal sizes/timing, no e-carb use, no ISF test (fasting correction without food/UAM), insulin peak not in profile beyond type name, dilution factor not numeric.

---

### Shared state (carry to step 2)
**Stable observations.** Good CGM; TIR high but CV and TBR matter; **night/early-morning TBR** and **late-afternoon TAR → evening TBR** are the two shapes; **no carbs in telemetry**; DynISF+UAM+SMB-always is the meal engine; scheduled basal ~16 U/d vs delivered ~20 U/d; GLP-1 and a mid-period profile/site change exist.

**Open competing causes (do not convert to a change yet).** Overnight basal vs target 90 vs evening IOB vs DynISF/SMB vs GLP-1. Afternoon peak vs unlogged meals vs 10:00 basal vs DynISF not aggressive enough until already high.

**Do not touch yet.** Any CR row; daytime basal increases; stronger ISF; anything that adds overnight insulin.

**Next workflow needs (step 2).** Review SMB/UAM interval, max SMB/UAM basal minutes, always-on SMB, DynISF 70%, Autosens off, max IOB/basal — as the more likely levers for UAM-driven days and overshoot lows — without treating them as a substitute for an untested basal cut.

**Stage statuses:** `data_quality` completed; `safety_overview` completed; `basal_targets` partial; `profile_cr_isf_dia` partial. No parameter decisions in this checkpoint.

response:
**CHECKPOINT 2 — AAPS automation**  
Decision-support only. No final JSON. Builds on CHECKPOINT 1. Shared state retained for step 3.

### AAPS inventory (category = aaps): **6 groups**
1. `aaps.core.smb_uam` — `smb_enabled=true`; `uam_enabled=true`  
2. `aaps.core.smb_activation` — `smb_always_enabled=true`; `smb_with_cob_enabled=false`; `smb_after_carbs_enabled=false`; `smb_with_temp_target_enabled=true`; `smb_with_high_temp_target_enabled=false`  
3. `aaps.core.smb_delivery` — `smb_interval_minutes=3 min`; `max_smb_basal_minutes=15 min`; `max_uam_smb_basal_minutes=20 min`  
4. `aaps.core.safety_limits` — `max_basal_u_per_hour=12 U/h`; `max_iob_units=25 U`  
5. `aaps.core.sensitivity` — `autosens_enabled=false`; `dynamic_sensitivity_enabled=true`; `autosens_raises_target=false`; `autosens_lowers_target=false`; `dynamic_isf_adjustment_factor_percent=70 %`  
6. `aaps.core.carb_absorption` — `min_5m_carbimpact=8 mg/dL/5 min`; `meal_max_absorption_hours=7 h`  

All listed component `current_value`s are present → later **verify is not available**; only **keep** or **change**. No `analysis_context.recent_results`.

**Note on remaining `raw_settings` (exceptions only).** Stock-like items (oref1, `free_peak_oref`, wizard %, form max bolus/carbs, default safety multipliers) are not treated as optimization knobs. Material points: loop reasons show **non-stock** behavior (UAM Boost 1/2, “UAM High Boost”, Enhanced oref1, G3 pre-UAM hold, twin/antBackout). On 14-Aug the enacted reason capped at **maxSafeBasal 4 U/h** while configured max basal is 12 — consistent with a multiplier × highest scheduled basal (0.8 × 5 = 4), so **12 U/h is not the binding cap**. `sensitivity_ratio` in samples is often 1 (neutral *adjustment*, not proof Autosens is off); Autosens is off because `autosens_enabled=false`. Reasons that mention “21m left” are remaining temp time, **not** the 3-minute SMB interval.

---

### 5. `automation_smb_uam` — **completed** | confidence **medium–high** on mechanism, **medium** on which single knob
**Links to CP1.** Zero carbs / `cob: 0` in every sampled loop status; daytime rise is UAM-shaped; evening TBR after afternoon TAR; do not raise overnight insulin until evening IOB is separated.

**Group 1 — SMB + UAM.** Both on is internally consistent with an unannounced-meal pattern. UAM is **not** treated as a second COB pool. This pair is the actual meal engine (CP1 H-P1).

**Group 2 — activation.** `smb_always_enabled=true` makes `smb_with_cob` / `smb_after_carbs` **inert**. High-TT SMB off matches repeated TT 135 (eating-soon / protective). SMB-with-TT on still allows SMB under non-high TTs (e.g. 15-Aug TT ~108). Net: SMB is available almost any time BG/UAM asks, except high TT.

**Group 3 — strength/frequency.** 3-minute interval is the aggressive part of the trio. Scheduled-basal math would cap SMB ≈ 15/60 × 0.5–0.8 ≈ **0.13–0.20 U** and UAM ≈ 20/60 × 0.5–0.8 ≈ **0.17–0.27 U**. Sampled reasons disagree: microbolus **0.3–0.4 U**, and 19-Aug 15:55 **SMB equals 1.6 U** with IOB already 4.73 U at BG 262. So **UAM minutes are not the observed size limiter** when boost / DynISF / effective basal are in play. `max_uam` (20) > `max_smb` (15) only matters if COB SMBs exist; here UAM is the binding path.

**Evidence.** Afternoon local TAR 20–32% (10:00–17:00) with COB 0 and UAM Boost language; same-day overshoots (14-Aug 234 → 56; 19-Aug 264 → 96; 13-Aug 172 → 47). Zero-temps appear when minGuardBG collapses (even negative in prediction). CGM coverage 98.7% — this is not a gap-driven SMB story.

**Is this compensating for profile?**  
- **Yes for CR:** unused CR + no carb entries → UAM/SMB substitute for meal insulin.  
- **Partly for afternoon basal/ISF:** highs begin before the 16:00 0.5 U/h step; DynISF already strengthens once high. Raising daytime basal or cutting CR would **stack** on always-on UAM.  
- **Creates overnight/evening hypo risk (CP1 H-S1–S3):** not compensating for high overnight basal; it is a plausible source of the IOB that hits target 90 at 23:00.

**Competing levers (do not move together).** Interval 3 min vs UAM 20 min vs always-on vs DynISF 70% can all explain the same late-day dump. Strongest *identifiable* automation signature is **always-on UAM at 3 min with boost sizes >> profile-basal SMB math**.

**Uncertainty / gaps.** Custom boost code means stock “15/20 min of basal” interpretation is incomplete. No full SMB time-series (24 loop samples). Cannot see whether 3 min is actually delivering every 3 min or often skipped by low-guard. TT 135 frequency may already be the user’s hypo mitigation.

**Constraint:** any later SMB change is **one** of {always-on, interval, UAM minutes} — not combined with DynISF or basal in the same step. Overnight basal cut remains blocked until this layer is considered.

---

### 6. `automation_sensitivity_limits` — **completed** | confidence **medium**
**Group 4 — max basal / max IOB.** 12 U/h and 25 U are present and far above TDD (~20 U/d) and scheduled basal (0.5–0.8). Observed peak IOB **4.7–5.9 U** never approached 25, so **max IOB is not the brake that failed**. Effective high temp was already limited (~4 U/h) in at least one enacted reason. These envelopes did not cause the hypos; they also did not prevent large UAM SMBs. Change is **unsupported as a first explanation** of CP1 patterns (keep-leaning unless a safety-envelope discussion is separated from dosing logic). Tightening them together with SMB/DynISF would violate “one dependent change.”

**Group 5 — Autosens / DynISF.** Internally consistent: Autosens off, both target-adjust flags off, DynISF on at **70%**. DynISF is the only live sensitivity adapter (CP1 H-P2). `variable_sens` ~28–124 vs seed ISF 56: stronger by day at highs (more insulin into the peak), weaker when low (so overnight TBR is a poor case for “flat 56 is too strong”). Afternoon TAR then 18–19 TBR fits **late, large DynISF-enabled UAM**, not missing Autosens. Enabling Autosens on top of DynISF would be a second adapter — not indicated. `sensitivity_ratio` 0.79–1.0 in samples is not treated as secret Autosens-on.

**Group 6 — carb absorption.** `min_5m_carbimpact=8` and `meal_max_absorption=7 h` have **no COB to act on**. Unused, not contradictory. Keep-leaning; do not retune absorption to “fix” UAM days. UAM ≠ duplicate carb absorption.

**Silent extras (safety, not routine knobs).** Default multipliers likely explain maxSafeBasal ~4 vs configured 12 — inconsistency of *display vs effective cap*, not a reason to retune multipliers. `min_carbs_required_grams=20` is idle with zero carb entries.

**Excessive IOB risk.** Real risk is **rate of IOB build via UAM+DynISF**, not the 25 U ceiling. 5.9 U IOB at 246 mg/dL with insulinReq 2.12 and SMB still firing is the concerning scene. CGM quality is good enough that this is algorithm/profile interaction, not junk BG.

**Is sensitivity compensating?** DynISF is compensating for a single flat ISF and for unlogged meals. It is also a candidate for overshoot (CP1 H-S3). It is **not** clearly compensating for a wrong overnight basal. Autosens-off is not a defect here.

**Uncertainty.** 70% vs “too high” cannot be isolated from 3-minute always-on UAM without a sequential test. GLP-1 notes (CP1) can mimic extra sensitivity in the evening.

---

### Shared state update (carry to step 3)
**Resolved enough to use.** Meal insulin ≈ UAM/SMB-always, not CR/COB. Carb-absorption settings are idle. Autosens is truly off; DynISF 70% is the sensitivity layer. Configured 12 U/h / 25 U IOB are slack envelopes; they are not the observed failure mode. High-TT SMB off is a protective consistency with TT 135.

**Still competing (do not convert to a bundle of changes).**  
1) Always-on UAM + 3 min interval stacking into evening.  
2) DynISF 70% collapsing ISF at highs.  
3) Evening residual IOB + target 90 ± mild overnight basal (CP1).  
4) GLP-1 / unlogged low intake.

**Keep-leaning unless step 3–4 finds a single separable test.** All six groups have values; idle groups (carb absorption, Autosens flags, max IOB/basal as first move) should stay **keep** if change is unsupported. If a change is later justified, **one** automation degree of freedom first (prefer the UAM delivery path over simultaneous DynISF + basal + ISF).

**Do not touch together.** SMB interval + UAM minutes + always-on; DynISF % + ISF seed; max basal + multipliers; any of the above + overnight basal or target.

**Step 3 need.** Meal/bolus strategy and e-carbs: with **zero** carb/e-carb telemetry, state whether the workable strategy is “UAM-only + protective TT” vs starting to announce carbs/e-carbs — without inventing meal composition.
